_model_map.note: where the sign code lives in the model (measured in JELAPANG element_psets, CIVIL_HIGHWAY_JELAPANG.md §K-6.1)

_cut_fill.status: SUGGESTED defaults (editable) — no standard gives them; tune reach_max_m per project
_cut_fill.note: Inferred cut/fill overlay (CIVIL_HIGHWAY_JELAPANG.md §INSPECT_EARTH_ROAD E1/E5): ground above the road on both sides = cut, below on both sides = fill. Fill is blue, not green, to avoid reading as vegetation (user 2026-10-09). reach_max_m caps the lateral spread; the tint stops earlier at daylight (ground meets road level).

_road_report.note: The Road Report cut-offs (CIVIL_HIGHWAY_JELAPANG.md §ROAD_REPORT). No standard gives prognosis cut-offs: drift_pct = chainage drift as % of the printed marker step (CRITICAL >= critical, WARNING >= warning); grade_window_m = chord length for grade and the shortest cut/fill stretch reported. The ATJ limits themselves come from the cited tables.

_chainage_map.note: where the chainage markers live in the model (CHAINAGE discipline = 332 glyph solids of 3D text, measured in CivilWorksPath.db, CIVIL_HIGHWAY_JELAPANG.md §CHAINAGE_GRID). drift_ok_m = route-vs-marker tolerance per interval; minor_m / major_m = tick spacing (Civil 3D / OpenRoads station style). Editable in Settings.

max_grade.note: one row per (table, terrain/area, speed). terrain_or_area "FLAT|I" = flat for rural classes, area type I for urban classes

geometric._user_editable: Everything below this note that is NOT extracted from ATJ 8/86 is an editable input or presentation choice; the Settings JSON editor overrides it (browser override + Reset). status "assumed" is shown as such on the legend and HUD until set to "user".

model_map.note: where the project title and the road surface live in the model (measured in CivilWorksPath element_psets / elements_meta)

rows.basis: title names federal routes (FT240 / FT005) = ATJ 8/86 Table 2.1 NETWORK "National network" (Highway or Expressway); Highway chosen — user to confirm

road_category_map.note: first row whose title_regex matches the model title wins; edit category to e.g. "Primary Road" / "Arterials" and set status "user"

area.note: not in the model — RURAL or URBAN (Table 2.4 / 3.2A vs 3.2B)

adt.note: projected ADT at design life (veh/day); Highway/Expressway rows of Table 2.4 need none; other categories do

area_type.note: ATJ 8/86 area type I / II / III — used for URBAN design speed (Table 3.2B) and grade (4.10x)

terrain_inputs.note: terrain per window = ATJ 8/86 class (thresholds 3% / 25% from the extracted terrain table) of the MEDIAN |gradient| of the long-section samples (A.civilProfile .ground, 1 m). window_m / min_pairs / assumed_terrain are assumed inputs. ATJ defines terrain by natural-ground CROSS-slope; the centre-line long section is the proxy (spec §SPEED_ZONES).

speed_setting.note: LEVER. derived = ATJ 8/86 chain. class = set "class" to R1-R6 / U1-U6 (speed, width, gradient from that class row). manual = set design_speed_kmh (all zones) or per_zone {"Z2": 70}; width/gradient looked up only if the speed identifies one class at that terrain, else "manual, no table row".

source.doc: NCHRP Report 672, Roundabouts: An Informational Guide, 2nd ed., TRB/FHWA 2010

roundabout.label: NCHRP 672 (US) — international reference, not JKR; ATJ 11/87 not in hand

nchrp_entry_speed._note: km/h = mph x 1.609344 rounded to integer; single-lane 20-25 mph, multilane 25-30 mph. Conservative demo = lower bound.

roundabout.approach_note: 'ssd_table_4_1' = ATJ 8/86 Table 4.1 stopping sight distance at the adjoining link design speed (before AND after the roundabout); or {"fixed_m": 150}. Demo rule, editable.
roundabout.sign_note: warning signs matched by name/code; logged beside the derived approach start for comparison only (not a boundary)

speed_ramp.note: presentation only (not from ATJ). Colour = linear RGB interpolation between stops by km/h, clamped at the ends: slowest (<=30) = very light warm white #fff3e0 (not pure white, so it still reads as painted on grey unpainted road), fastest = strong red #b71c1c. Lightness decreases monotonically with speed. Editable.

geometric.node_kinds_note: controlled-node kinds handled by ONE engine mechanism (speed_zones.js §CONTROLLED_NODE); each key has its own config object below. Add a kind = add a config + model_map keys, no code.

signal_junction.label: demo default — not from a standard
signal_junction.speed_note: No free standard gives a signalised-junction speed (ATJ 11/87 not in hand; US FHWA signal guides do not reduce design speed): conservative demo default, editable.
signal_junction.approach_note: 'ssd_table_4_1' = ATJ 8/86 Table 4.1 stopping sight distance at the adjoining link design speed (a driver must be able to stop for a red light), each side that exists; or {"fixed_m": 150}.
signal_junction.sign_note: warning signs matched by name/code; logged beside the derived approach start for comparison only (not a boundary)

geometric.disc_note: speed-limit discs: a zone START with no speed sign within disc_has_sign_m (chainage) borrows the nearest SIGNAGE board within disc_snap_m (dashed amber 'no speed sign - borrowed'); none in range -> free-standing marker. Flags the missing RP. 7 for engineers.

zone_tags._note: short legend/list tag per provenance class; the full provenance stays in the row tooltip + HUD card (user 2026-10-08). Tags: derived (ATJ chain) · demo (editable demo rule) · NCHRP 672 (international reference) · user (lever).

size_vs_speed.finding: No speed-banded SIGN-BOARD size table exists in ATJ 2A/2B. The only speed-banded size tables are LETTER HEIGHT for guide signs / gantries / camera boxes (needs lettering, which the model does not carry). WD.39a/39b chevron sizes are three options (900x750, 750x600, 600x450 mm) with NO speed mapping in the text (speed/km/h in the WD.39 block: False). 2B p.56 shape sizes (min/normal width per shape) are not speed-banded.
